lead_with.title: From library hits to better binders
lead_with.text: His pipeline produces VHH hits from synthetic libraries. MAbSilico can **optimize affinity, stability and developability** of the best hits in silico in **~21 days**, then confirm by **BLI / cytometry / HTRF**.

lead_with.title: Targets that are hard to hit
lead_with.text: Cell-type-specific targeting in the retina needs **epitope-specific** binders. Offer epitope-directed design on one target where selections struggle.

lead_with.title: Collaborate on funding
lead_with.text: Propose a joint **Horizon Europe / Swiss (SNSF, Innosuisse)** application — MAbSilico has EU-consortium experience; a low-cash way for an academic platform to work with industry.

company.text: IOB (Basel) unites researchers and clinicians to understand eye diseases and develop new therapies, with strong genetics, single-cell and gene-therapy work on the retina. The Protein Engineering Platform gives IOB scientists access to highly specific binders used to target therapies to specific retinal cell types. Founded 2017 by Novartis, the University Hospital Basel and the University of Basel; funded by foundations and public grants.

financials.text: Research foundation — no revenue figures. Budget comes from founders, foundations and grants: expect **small paid pilots or grant-funded collaborations**, not large service contracts.

talking_points: Which targets are you selecting VHHs against today, and where do selections struggle (affinity, specificity, stability)?
How many maturation rounds does a typical lead need now? Would in silico optimization of your top hits save time?
Do you need **humanized** VHHs for therapeutic use, or binders for targeting/vectors?
Would a small pilot on one VHH lead, validated by your assays plus our BLI/cytometry, be useful?
Are you planning grant applications (Horizon Europe, SNSF, Innosuisse) where a partner like MAbSilico could join?
Who else at IOB should join — PIs who use your binders?
